summary: This clipped page from the Arlington Behavior Therapy (Psychotherapy) blog contains several short psychology articles plus a practice news item. Topics include 15 science-backed tips for achieving goals using CBT principles, why therapy may still help treatment non-responders, strategies for managing uncertainty and worry, factors other than ADHD that cause attention problems, the 2023 Arlington Best Business award, and mistakes that keep lonely people isolated. The note is truncated mid-article in the loneliness piece.
one_line: Clipped Arlington Behavior Therapy blog page covering goal-setting tips, therapy for non-responders, managing uncertainty, attention problems, the business award, and loneliness.
key_facts: The goal-setting article lists 15 strategies drawn from cognitive behavioral therapy principles, including 'Monitor your progress' and 'Be a teacher.'
Study authors reviewed 18 psychotherapy randomized control trials involving 1,734 nonresponders, published in Clinical Psychology Review by Andrew Gloster in Switzerland.
The article states that 30 to 40 percent of people cannot recover after first-line mental health treatment; these people are called non-responders.
The non-responder article says no differences in outcomes were found based on psychotherapy type, but ACT, MBCT, and DBT had a particularly significant impact on reducing symptoms.
The uncertainty article attributes the 'impact bias' to psychologists Daniel Gilbert and Timothy Wilson from Harvard.
The uncertainty article suggests scheduling a daily worry time of 20 minutes and recommends rating situations on 'an imaginary uncertainty scale between zero and 100.'
Diaphragmatic breathing is described as placing one hand on the stomach and another on the chest for seven minutes.
The ADHD article states that 1 in 5 children with ADHD were improperly diagnosed by doctors, according to a study by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
The ADHD article cites a Pew Research Center study conducted from Jan. 25 to Feb. 8, 2021, finding 31 percent of U.S. adults are online 'almost constantly.'
Sleep scientist Charles A. Czeisler, professor of sleep medicine at Harvard Medical School, says focused attention is one of the first things to go when people lose sleep.

The award article reports the Arlington/DC Behavior Therapy Institute was honored as the 2023 Service Business of the Year at the Arlington Chamber of Commerce's 37th Annual Arlington Best Business Awards on May 16, 2023 at the Army Navy Country Club.
Kate Bates, Arlington Chamber President & CEO, called the award 'a testament to their business success and delivery of exceptional quality and service.'
The loneliness article reports that in a September Pew Research Center survey, 42 percent of Americans reported feeling lonely at least once or twice during the past week.
The loneliness article cites the 85-year-long Harvard Study of Adult Development, which found social connections were among the strongest predictors of happiness and health.
